# git-graph

git-graph is a command line tool to visualize Git history graphs in a
comprehensible way, following different branching models.

Overview

Run the tool inside a Git repository to display a structured view of commit
history and branching. For example:

    git-graph

For a specific branching model (predefined or user-provided), use:

    git-graph --model simple

For full CLI options and detailed documentation, see docs/manual.md.

Installation

Download a pre-compiled binary for your platform from the project's
releases and place it on your PATH. Alternatively, use your system's
package manager if a packaged release is available.

License

This project is provided under the terms of the LICENSE file included in
this repository.

--- MANUAL ---
# git-graph manual

**Content**

* [Overview](#overview)
* [Options](#options)
* [Formatting](#formatting)
* [Custom branching models](#custom-branching-models)

## Overview

The most basic usage is to simply call git-graph from inside a Git repository:

```
git-graph
```

This works also deeper down the directory tree, so no need to be in the repository's root folder.

Alternatively, the path to the repository to visualize can be specified with option `--path`:

```
git-graph --path "path/to/repo"
```

**Branching models**

The above call assumes the GitFlow branching model (the default). Different branching models can be used with the option `--model` or `-m`:

```
git-graph --model simple
```

To *permanently* set the branching model for a repository, use subcommand `model`, like

```
git-graph model simple
```

Use the subcommand without argument to view the currently set branching model of a repository:

```
git-graph model
```

To view all available branching models, use option `--list` or `-l` of the subcommand:

```
git-graph model --list
```

For **defining your own models**, see section [Custom branching models](#custom-branching-models).

**Styles**

Git-graph supports different styles. Besides the default `normal` (alias `thin`), supported styles are `round`, `bold`, `double` and `ascii`. Use a style with option `--style` or `-s`:

```
git-graph --style round
```

![styles](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44003176/103467621-357ce780-4d51-11eb-8ff9-dd7be8b40f84.png)

Style `ascii` can be used for devices and media that do not support Unicode/UTF-8 characters. 

**Formatting**

Git-graph supports predefined as well as custom commit formatting through option `--format`. Available presets follow Git: `oneline` (the default), `short`, `medium` and `full`. For details and custom formatting, see section [Formatting](#formatting).

For a complete list of all available options, see the next section [Options](#options).

## Options

All options are explained in the CLI help. View it with `git-graph -h`:

```

## Formatting

Formatting can be specified with the `--format` option.

Predefined formats are `oneline` (the default), `short`, `medium` and `full`. They should behave like the Git formatting presets described in the [Git documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/pretty-formats).

**oneline**

```
<hash> [<refs>] <title line>
```

**short**

```
commit <hash> [<refs>]
Author: <author>

<title line>
```

**medium**

```
commit <hash> [<refs>]
Author: <author>
Date:   <author date>

<title line>

<full commit message>
```

**full**

```
commit <hash> [<refs>]
Author: <author>
Commit: <committer>
Date:   <author date>

<title line>

<full commit message>
```

### Custom formatting

Formatting strings use a subset of the placeholders available in `git log --format="..."`:

| Placeholder | Replaced with                               |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| %n          | newline                                     |
| %H          | commit hash                                 |
| %h          | abbreviated commit hash                     |
| %P          | parent commit hashes                        |
| %p          | abbreviated parent commit hashes            |
| %d          | refs (branches, tags)                       |
| %s          | commit summary                              |
| %b          | commit message body                         |
| %B          | raw body (subject and body)                 |
| %an         | author name                                 |
| %ae         | author email                                |
| %ad         | author date                                 |
| %as         | author date in short format `YYYY-MM-DD`    |
| %ar         | author date, relative format (e.g., "21 hours ago") |
| %cn         | committer name                              |
| %ce         | committer email                             |
| %cd         | committer date                              |
| %cs         | committer date in short format `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| %cr         | committer date, relative format (e.g., "4 days ago") |

If you add a '+' (plus sign) after % of a placeholder, a line-feed is inserted immediately before the expansion if and only if the placeholder expands to a non-empty string.

If you add a '-' (minus sign) after % of a placeholder, all consecutive line-feeds immediately preceding the expansion are deleted if and only if the placeholder expands to an empty string.

If you add a ' ' (space) after % of a placeholder, a space is inserted immediately before the expansion if and only if the placeholder expands to a non-empty string.

See also the [Git documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/pretty-formats).

More formatting placeholders are planned for later releases.

# Overview

To generate a graph, [GitGraph::new()] will read the repository
and assign every commit to a single branch.

It takes the following steps to generate the graph

- Identify branches
- Sort branches by persistence
- Trace branches to commits
- Filtering and indexing

## Identify branches
Local and remote git-branches and tags are used as candidates for branches.
A branch can be identified by a merge commit, even though no current git-branch
refers to it.

## Sort branches by persistence
Each branch is assigned a persistence which can be configured by settings.
Think of persistence as z-order where lower values take preceedence.

branch starts with a head, and follow the primary parent while it is
available. It stops when the parent is a commit already assigned to a branch.

class Branch:
    name: str
    head: object
    number: int
    kind: str
    persistence: int = 0

    color: int = 7
    svg_color: str = 'gray'

    merge: object = None
    priority: int = 1000000000
    start: object = None
    end: object = None
    source: object = None
    target: object = None
    column: int = 99
    commits: list = field(default_factory=list)

    def __init__(self,repo,model):
        self.repo=repo
        self.model=model
        self.commits=repo.commits
        self.by_id=repo.by_id
        self.branches=[]
        self.ref_branches={}

            b=self.make_branch(r.name,self.by_id[r.oid],r.number,r.kind)
            self.branches.append(b)
            self.ref_branches[id(r)]=b
        original=list(self.branches)
        number=max([r.number for r in repo.refs]+[0])
        inferred=[]
        reused=set()

            if len(c.parents)<2 or c.parents[1] not in self.by_id:continue
            head=self.by_id[c.parents[1]]
            name=self.merge_name(c.summary)
            reuse=next((b for b in original if b.name==name and b.head is head and head.index==c.index+1),None)
            if reuse:
                reuse.priority=min(reuse.priority,c.index)
                reused.add(reuse)
                continue
            # Separate sightings of an already identified head denote the same
            # branch; retain the most recent merge as its visible beginning.
            if any(b.head is head and b.name==name for b in inferred):continue
            number+=1
            b=self.make_branch(name,head,number,'merge')
            b.implicit=True;b.merge=c;b.priority=c.index
            inferred.append(b)
        all_branches=inferred+original
        self.branches=sorted(all_branches,key=lambda b:b.persistence)
        trace_order=sorted(all_branches,key=lambda b:(b.persistence,b.priority))
        for b in trace_order:
            c=b.head
            if c.branch is not None:continue
            b.start=b.merge.index+1 if b.implicit else c.index
            while c is not None and c.branch is None:
                c.branch=b;b.commits.append(c)
                if not c.parents:
                    b.end=c.index
                    break
                p=self.by_id.get(c.parents[0])
                if p is None:break
                if p.branch is not None:
                    b.end=p.index-1
                    b.source=p.branch.order
                    break
                c=p

        if len(kept)!=len(self.commits):
            old_indices=[c.index for c in kept]
            for b in self.branches:
                if b.start is not None:b.start=sum(i<b.start for i in old_indices)
                if b.end is not None:b.end=sum(i<=b.end for i in old_indices)-1
            self.commits=kept
            self.by_id={c.oid:c for c in kept}
            for i,c in enumerate(kept):c.index=i

        for c in self.commits:
            b=c.branch
            if len(c.parents)>1:

                if p and p.branch is not b:
                    if b.source is None:b.source=p.branch.order

        b.order=self.model.group(name,'order')

        return 'unknown'

            t=b.order if b.target is None else b.target
            end=n if b.end is None else b.end
            return (max(s,t),end-b.start,b.start)
        for b in sorted((b for b in self.branches if b.start is not None),key=key):

            index=0
            while index<len(lanes) and any(not(end<a or start>z) for a,z in lanes[index]):index+=1
            if index==len(lanes):lanes.append([])
            lanes[index].append((start,end))
            b.column=index
        offset=0
        for group in sorted(occupied):
            for b in self.branches:
                if b.start is not None and b.order==group:b.column+=offset
            offset+=len(occupied[group])
        self.columns=offset

        def opt(n):return 'None' if n is None else f'Some({n})'
        return ''.join(f'{b.name} (col {b.column}) (({opt(b.start)}, {opt(b.end)})) '+('m' if b.implicit else '')+f' s: {opt(b.source)}, t: {opt(b.target)}\n' for b in self.branches)

        self.branches=[]
        self.ref_branches={}
        for r in repo.refs:
            b=self.make_branch(r.name,self.by_id[r.oid],r.number,r.kind)
            self.branches.append(b)
            self.ref_branches[id(r)]=b
        original=list(self.branches)
        number=max([r.number for r in repo.refs]+[0])
        inferred=[]
        reused=set()
        for c in self.commits:
            if len(c.parents)<2 or c.parents[1] not in self.by_id:continue
            head=self.by_id[c.parents[1]]
            name=self.merge_name(c.summary)
            reuse=next((b for b in original if b.name==name and b.head is head and head.index==c.index+1),None)
            if reuse:
                reuse.priority=min(reuse.priority,c.index)
                reused.add(reuse)
                continue
            # Separate sightings of an already identified head denote the same
            # branch; retain the most recent merge as its visible beginning.
            if any(b.head is head and b.name==name for b in inferred):continue
            number+=1
            b=self.make_branch(name,head,number,'merge')
            b.implicit=True;b.merge=c;b.priority=c.index
            inferred.append(b)
        all_branches=inferred+original
        self.branches=sorted(all_branches,key=lambda b:b.persistence)
        trace_order=sorted(all_branches,key=lambda b:(b.persistence,b.priority))
        for b in trace_order:
            c=b.head
            if c.branch is not None:continue
            b.start=b.merge.index+1 if b.implicit else c.index
            while c is not None and c.branch is None:
                c.branch=b;b.commits.append(c)
                if not c.parents:
                    b.end=c.index
                    break
                p=self.by_id.get(c.parents[0])
                if p is None:break
                if p.branch is not None:
                    b.end=p.index-1
                    b.source=p.branch.order
                    break
                c=p
        # Drop commits reachable only through a detached, unreferenced HEAD.
        kept=[c for c in self.commits if c.branch is not None]
        if len(kept)!=len(self.commits):
            old_indices=[c.index for c in kept]
            for b in self.branches:
                if b.start is not None:b.start=sum(i<b.start for i in old_indices)
                if b.end is not None:b.end=sum(i<=b.end for i in old_indices)-1
            self.commits=kept
            self.by_id={c.oid:c for c in kept}
            for i,c in enumerate(kept):c.index=i
        # Gather source/target ordering information from cross-branch edges.
        for c in self.commits:
            b=c.branch
            if len(c.parents)>1:
                p=self.by_id.get(c.parents[1])
                if p and p.branch is not b:
                    if b.source is None:b.source=p.branch.order
        for b in self.branches:
            if b.implicit and b.merge and b.merge.branch:
                b.target=b.merge.branch.order
        self.assign_columns()

    def make_branch(self,name,head,number,kind):
        b=Branch(name,head,number,kind)
        b.persistence=self.model.group(name,'persistence')
        b.order=self.model.group(name,'order')
        b.color=self.model.color(name,number)
        b.svg_color=self.model.color(name,number,True)
        return b

    @staticmethod
    def merge_name(summary):
        # The usual branch and remote-tracking merge messages also survive
        # deletion of the corresponding refs.
        m=re.search(r"Merge (?:remote-tracking )?branch '([^']+)'",summary)
        if m:
            name=m[1]
            if re.search(r" of \S+",summary[m.end():]):name='fork/'+name
            return name
        return 'unknown'

    def assign_columns(self):
        n=len(self.commits)
        occupied={}
        def key(b):
            s=b.order if b.source is None else b.source
            t=b.order if b.target is None else b.target
            end=n if b.end is None else b.end
            return (max(s,t),end-b.start,b.start)
        for b in sorted((b for b in self.branches if b.start is not None),key=key):
            lanes=occupied.setdefault(b.order,[])
            start=b.start;end=n if b.end is None else b.end
            index=0
            while index<len(lanes) and any(not(end<a or start>z) for a,z in lanes[index]):index+=1
            if index==len(lanes):lanes.append([])
            lanes[index].append((start,end))
            b.column=index
        offset=0
        for group in sorted(occupied):
            for b in self.branches:
                if b.start is not None and b.order==group:b.column+=offset
            offset+=len(occupied[group])
        self.columns=offset

    def debug(self):
        def opt(n):return 'None' if n is None else f'Some({n})'
        return ''.join(f'{b.name} (col {b.column}) (({opt(b.start)}, {opt(b.end)})) '+('m' if b.implicit else '')+f' s: {opt(b.source)}, t: {opt(b.target)}\n' for b in self.branches)

"""Black-box regression tests using small, independently constructed repositories."""
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PROGRAM = Path(os.environ.get('EXECUTABLE', str(ROOT / 'executable'))).resolve()


class GraphTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.base = Path(self.temp.name)
        self.repo = self.base / 'repo'
        self.repo.mkdir()
        self.env = dict(os.environ, XDG_CONFIG_HOME=str(self.base / 'config'),
                        GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM='1', GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL='/dev/null')
        self.git('init', '-q', '-b', 'main')
        self.git('config', 'user.name', 'Alice Example')
        self.git('config', 'user.email', 'alice@example.com')

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def git(self, *args, env=None):
        p = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(self.repo), *args], env=env or self.env,
                           stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, check=True)
        return p.stdout.decode().strip()

    def dated(self, day):
        date = f'2020-01-{day:02}T12:34:56+0230'
        return dict(self.env, GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=date, GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=date)

    def commit(self, message, day):
        self.git('commit', '--allow-empty', '-q', '-m', message, env=self.dated(day))
        return self.git('rev-parse', 'HEAD')

    def run_tool(self, *args):
        return subprocess.run([str(PROGRAM), *args], cwd=self.repo, env=self.env,
                              stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)

    def output(self, *args):
        p = self.run_tool(*args)
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0, p.stderr.decode())
        return p.stdout.decode()

    def linear(self):
        root = self.commit('Initial subject', 1)
        body = self.commit('Second subject\n\nBody first line.\nBody second line.\n\nLast paragraph.', 2)
        self.git('tag', 'v1.0')
        tip = self.commit('Third subject', 3)
        return root, body, tip

    def merged(self):
        root = self.commit('Root', 1)
